ai-harness.titulo: AI harness: who does the AI's work

inicio.kicker: LOOP-R Engineering Track · course 0 of 6 · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: Base: the anatomy of an agent loop that works, checks itself, and knows when to stop
inicio.lead: Goal, state, action, verification, and stop. The harness around the model, today's loop engines and the limits of each, LOOP-R with its nine agents, done criterion from 0 to 4, and caps. Each lesson points to the track course that goes deeper on the topic.
inicio.capa_alt: Dark workbench with a braided cable looped in a knot, a laptop showing a terminal, and a panel with two gauges.

cursos.sub: This is course 0. Each lesson here points to the course that owns the topic. Suggested order: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5.

itens.l: The five parts, the harness, loop engines, LOOP-R, done criterion from 0 to 4, and caps.
A separate, skeptical evaluator, frozen tests, reward hacking, the gold set, and a calibrated judge.
The seven-file kit, goal.md level 3+, context in bands, handoff, headless loop, and measurement.
When not to use it, subagents, generator × evaluator, worktrees, queues, and the Claude + Codex team.
Lethal trifecta, Rule of Two, injection through the content it reads, guard hooks and sandbox.
Hypothesis with a number, experiment, promotion and rollback, lessons, and the risk of optimizing against the meter.

inicio.aulas_sub: From concept to your first running loop: the pieces, what sits around the model, the engines, LOOP-R, state, criterion, caps, and the final practice.

itens: People who already use Claude Code or Codex in the terminal and want the agent to work on its own for more than one turn.
People who have seen the agent say "done" with no proof, or spin on the same error until the quota runs out.
People who will take the LOOP-R Engineering Track and need the shared vocabulary of the six courses.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Point out the five pieces in any loop and say which one is missing.
Choose between /goal, /loop, Ralph, routines and codex exec based on what each one does and doesn't do.
Rate a done criterion from 0 to 4 and rewrite the vague one up to level 3.
Run your first loop with frozen tests, a turn cap and proof in the output.
Linux or macOS with bash, git and Python 3 (pytest for lesson 8).
Claude Code or Codex installed and signed in through your subscription. The practices in lessons 1, 5 and 7 don't use any quota.
No previous course needed: this is the entry point of the track.
